title: Inert etale comparisons descend to etale quotient comparisons
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group acting on separated locally Noetherian schemes $U,V$, each covered by invariant affine opens, and let $h:V\to U$ be a $G$-equivariant etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For a geometric point $v$ put $G_v=\{g:g\circ v=v\}$. The locus on which $G_v=G_{h(v)}$ is an invariant open subset of $V$. Restrict to this locus (so $h$ is called inert). Suppose $q_U:U\to U/G$ and $q_V:V\to V/G$ are finite surjective scheme quotients with orbit geometric fibres and invariant structure sheaves. Then $\bar h:V/G\to U/G$ is etale, and
$$V\simeq U\times_{U/G}(V/G)$$
compatibly with the quotient maps and $G$-actions. These assertions hold locally on the quotients, so apply to pointed etale neighborhoods and are compatible with composition.

In addition suppose $M_U,M_V$ are fs log structures [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], $h$ is strict, both actions are very tame, and their quotient log structures are $N_U=(q_{U*}M_U)^G$ and $N_V=(q_{V*}M_V)^G$. Here strict means that the source log structure is pulled back from the target; very tame means that geometric stabilizers have invertible order and act trivially on the characteristic monoid and the strict local log stratum (the quotient of the strict local ring by the images of nonunit log sections). Then $\bar h$ is strict for $N_V,N_U$.
